description: Python toolkit for reading, writing, and lazily transforming unit-aware data from cosmological simulations (HACC) produced by Argonne National Laboratory's CPAC group. Reads HDF5 with full cosmological unit awareness and materializes datasets to Astropy and NumPy; supports HEALPix maps, spatial queries, structure/lightcone collections, and MPI.
rules: The entry point is `import opencosmo as oc` and `ds = oc.open("file.hdf5")`. Open collections of related datasets with the same call.

All transformations are lazy and return a new immutable Dataset or Collection; nothing is read from disk until you materialize. Chain transformations (with_units, filter, select, take, sort_by, bound, with_new_columns) to produce expressions

Data from Dataset and Lightcone objects can be retrieved with `dataset.get_data()`. It is generally unwise to access data directly from a StructureCollection, especially if it contains particles. However collection's dataset can be accessed by, for example `collection["halo_properties"].get_data()`

Build column expressions with `oc.col("column_name")` and use them in `filter`, `select`, and `with_new_columns`, e.g. `ds.filter(oc.col("fof_halo_mass") > 1e13)`. Do not use pandas-style boolean indexing or `df[...]` access.

Unit conventions are set with `ds.with_units(convention)` where convention is one of 'physical', 'comoving', 'scalefree', or 'unitless'. The default is `comoving`, which does not include factors of little h. Filters are evaluated in the dataset's current convention
`select` picks a subset of columns, adds derived columns, or returns scalar summary statistics. `take(n, at='random'|'start'|'end')` selects rows. `bound(region)` restricts to a spatial region.
`evaluate` runs a computation over every row of a dataset or collection.
After transforming data, it can be written to an `opencosmo` file with `oc.write`

Materialize with `get_data()` (default Astropy). Convert to other containers via the appropriate output option — NumPy, pandas, Polars, Arrow, or JAX are all supported. Only numpy and astropy are available by default. You must install the relevant libraries for other output formats.

Requires Python 3.12+. Optional MPI support is enabled via the `mpi` extra (mpi4py); the same lazy API works across ranks. Scripts that run in a single thread should run with no modifications in an MPI environment

The top-level public api functions are `open`, `write`, `col`, `make_box`, `make_cone`, and `make_skybox`. The top-level user-facing objects are `Dataset`, `Lightcone`, `StructureCollection`, and `SimulationCollection`. All non-underscored methods on these objects are part of the public API. Do not import and use functions from other locations, execpt analysis tools

The `opencosmo.analysis` tools contain additional user-facing analysis tools for performing useful operations such as producing images and plots, or computing statistcs. They may require additiona dependencies.
